title: Must & Mustn't
description: State strong rules and prohibitions clearly.
objectives: State strong rules and prohibitions clearly.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to state strong rules and prohibitions clearly. The central language is must and mustn't for rules. It belongs to the practical context of work, study & responsibilities. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: Visitors must sign in at reception.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the must & mustn't exchange.
This must & mustn't model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: What do you need to do?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the must & mustn't exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “Visitors must sign in at reception.” and “You mustn't share your password.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: must and mustn't for rules.
